exposure: glucose response trajectories (moderate increase following decrease, sustained low-level increase, moderate increase following slow decrease, rapid increase following slow decrease)
GDM subtypes (isolated fasting hyperglycemia, isolated post-load hyperglycemia, combined hyperglycemia)
cohort: The study included 5348 women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) who underwent oral glucose tolerance tests during pregnancy (24-28 weeks) and postpartum (4-12 weeks).
finding: Distinct gestational oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) response patterns, including individual time-point glucose values, glucose trajectories, and GDM subtypes, are associated with varying risks of postpartum glucose intolerance in women with GDM.
